correctness.rationale: For S(1^a,2^b) with integers a>=1,b>=2, the target inner long-arm vertex x_1 has eccentricity three. A stack of >=4 anywhere cannot end at x_1; a short leaf receiving >=3 cups is fatal because its only distance-three exit reaches a long-arm end and would create >=4 cups. Each short leaf must therefore either send its untouched one cup to center c or receive the lone original cup of c; after c empties it never refills, and after two unit-leaf incoming moves it has >=3 cups with eccentricity two, so two short leaves cannot both be cleared. For a=1 the four target orbits (c, short leaf, x_1, y_1) have explicit all-occupied legal sequences including parity-dependent b and all finish in 2b+1 moves. Independent BFS graph distances and complete replay checked 236 positive orbit representatives for every b from 2 through 60 and all four target types; independent full state graph obstruction exploration at six small (a,b) combinations found no path to x_1. The symbolic bottleneck/construction proves all unbounded a,b, not finite interpolation.

originality.rationale: The primary 2023 cup-stacking paper introduces game and expressly leaves mixed short/long spider cases open aside from the one-long-arm subfamily, while proving all arms length >=2. A 2024 Hamilton-path sufficient condition is inapplicable because these spiders have >=3 leaves, and it addresses different graph families. The specific a=1 iff classification with b>=2 uses new obstruction and constructive parity sequences. An original Veselovac thesis and possible later unindexed solution remain priority risks.
